mitre.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Symmetric Encrypted Non-C2 Protocol

description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a symmetrically encrypted network protocol other than that of the existing command and control channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main command and control server. Symmetric encryption algorithms are those that use shared keys between the sender and receiver. To enable encryption, adversaries may build the symmetric key into the malware. Tools such as dnscat2 establish a session over DNS where the payload is encrypted with a session key derived during a Diffie-Hellman handshake (Salsa20), then encoded into subdomain labels.
artifacts: DNS A / TXT / CNAME query patterns inconsistent with normal browsing behavior
DNS traffic to non-corporate / non-resolver IP addresses (direct DNS to a controlled server on UDP/53)
TXT or CNAME responses carrying encrypted payload bytes from the controlled DNS server
long-lived UDP/53 conversation between a single client and a single external server
high entropy in DNS query labels (encrypted dnscat2 traffic — distinguishes from plain hex/base32 encoding)
dnscat2 session establishment handshake (DH key exchange) followed by encrypted MSG packets

pcaps.name: Internal DNS exfiltration small payload - dnscat2
pcaps.description: Internal DNS tunneling exfiltration of a small payload using dnscat2 between a client and a controlled DNS listener for the exfil.packetfeeder.lab zone, showing encrypted DNS traffic on UDP/53 with high-entropy subdomain labels.

pcaps.name: Internal DNS exfiltration large payload - dnscat2
pcaps.description: Internal DNS tunneling exfiltration of a large payload using dnscat2 between a client and a controlled DNS listener for the exfil.packetfeeder.lab zone, showing a sustained high-volume encrypted DNS conversation on UDP/53 with high-entropy subdomain labels.
